thread:
emily: Heads-up — hit a nasty HF->Redwood chat_template conversion edgecase: marker tokens straddle a role boundary and sometimes the role label disappears after render when the jinja var is empty.

raj: Can you paste the minimal jinja snippet that reproduces it?

emily: Sure — here's the template we take from the model repo (simplified):

emily: ```jinja
{% if system_prompt %}SYSTEM: {{ system_prompt }}
{% endif %}
{% for msg in conversation %}
{{ msg.role }}: {{- msg.content -}}
{% endfor %}
```

cole: Interesting — you're using `{{- ... -}}` whitespace control. If a `msg.content` is empty that can remove the separating space/newline and glue the colon into the next token. Did you see the rendered string?

emily: Yep. Example render when the assistant reply is empty: 

emily: ```text
SYSTEM: Keep responses short
user: Tell me a joke
assistant:  
user: Follow-up question
```

emily: After tokenizing (tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...)) we get: 

emily: ```text
..., 'assistant:', 'user:', ...
```

emily: But with the `{{- msg.content -}}` control the `assistant:` marker sometimes gets attached to the trailing token of the previous line during byte-level splitting, which downstream code that searches for role prefixes misses.

taylor: :thinking: That matches a bug I saw where role detection uses simple string scans for `^assistant:` etc. If there's no explicit separator, the regex fails. Two obvious fixes: (1) in the converter always emit an explicit sentinel between role and content (e.g. `<|role|>`), or (2) never use `-` whitespace squashing for chat templates translated to Redwood prompts.

raj: Do we have tests that include empty `assistant` messages? I think our HF->Redwood conversion suite missed that.

emily: No, we didn't. It was caught by manual eval when onboarding the new int4 quantized variant — quality regressed on role alignment tests. The quantized model made tokenization more brittle so the role-swap bug surfaced.

cole: Yikes. Short-term patch: when converting, insert the ASCII sentinel `|||SEP|||` between role label and content (and add it to `additional_special_tokens` for the tokenizer). That way token boundaries are preserved even post-quantization. Longer-term: add a canonical sentinel token and id mapping in the model config.

emily: Example converter diff I'll try: 

emily: ```diff
-    out += f"{role}: {rendered}\n"
+    out += f"{role}: |||SEP||| {rendered}\n"
```

emily: And tokenizer update: `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'additional_special_tokens': ['|||SEP|||']})`

taylor: Also add a unit test in `tests/conversion/test_empty_roles.py` with a few permutations: empty assistant, empty user, trailing whitespace, and a long prefix that forces token split. Make sure eval harness checks we still detect role boundaries after tokenization+quantization.

raj: Agreed. Can you also log an eval run comparing pre/post conversion on our microbench: `evals/role-alignment/{model}/{quant}.yaml` so we can see regression numbers?

emily: Will do. Planning to open PR with converter + tokenizer patch + tests. I'll add an eval config and run the harness on the int4 candidate.

deploy-bot: CI queued for branch emily/sep-sentinel (build 1124). :eyes:

cole: Thanks — once you have the PR link drop it here and I'll add a quick review for the tokenizer changes. Also let's add a short note in the onboarding checklist about "rendered-empty-role-guards" so new models don't regress on this.

emily: Will do. Thanks all. :+1:
